nodes.label: RIEMANN-BENCH: Research-Level Mathematics Benchmark
nodes.author: Suhaas Garre, Erik Knutsen, Sushant Mehta, Edwin Chen
nodes.rationale: Private benchmark of 25 expert-curated PhD-level mathematics problems; all frontier models score below 10% despite access to coding tools and search, revealing gap between olympiad-level and research-level reasoning.

nodes.label: RIEMANN-BENCH Problem Construction
nodes.rationale: 25 problems authored by Ivy League professors, graduate students, and PhD-holding IMO medalists; each took weeks to solve independently; require unambiguous closed-form solutions with programmatic verification.

nodes.label: Double-Blind Verification Protocol
nodes.rationale: Two independent domain experts solve each problem from scratch without seeing author's solution; assess quality for ambiguity, underspecification, and difficulty calibration; problems failing verification are revised or excluded.

nodes.label: Private Benchmark Design
nodes.rationale: Dataset kept strictly private to prevent leakage and contamination; labs submit models through controlled evaluation service; ensures measured performance reflects authentic capability rather than memorization.

nodes.label: Unconstrained Agent Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Models given full access to Python interpreter, search, and open-ended reasoning with no artificial constraints; reflects genuine research setting; 100 independent runs per problem with unbiased pass@ estimator.

nodes.label: Hahn Series Multibasic Modules Classification Problem
nodes.rationale: Classification of multibasic A-modules over Hahn series ring; requires deep familiarity with valuation theory, tensor-hom adjunction, ring theory, and combinatorial case analysis; estimated 40-50 hours to solve from scratch.

nodes.label: Frontier Models Evaluated (7)
nodes.rationale: Gemini 3.1 Pro (6%), Claude Opus 4.6 (6%), Gemini 3 Pro (4%), Kimi K2.5 (4%), DeepSeek V3.2 (3%), GPT 5.2 (2%), Claude Opus 4.5 (2%); all below 10% pass@1.

nodes.label: Unbiased Pass@k Estimator
nodes.rationale: Chen et al. (2021) estimator computing pass rates from n=100 independent attempts; provides unbiased measurements of model capability at any sampling budget k; ensures stable, reproducible difficulty assessments.

nodes.label: Representative Model Failure Analysis
nodes.rationale: Model substituted inapplicable 'generalized scales' framework for A-module theory; fabricated nonexistent theorem (M. Getz, Theorem 4.14); produced structurally coherent but substantively wrong reasoning chain with answer off by orders of magnitude.

nodes.label: Olympiad vs. Research-Level Mathematics Distinction
nodes.rationale: IMO problems reward lateral thinking with elementary tools, solvable in hours; research problems demand deep theory, multi-step reasoning, weeks of effort; saturation of competition benchmarks does not imply mathematical reasoning is solved.

nodes.label: AI-Assisted Mathematical Research Paradigm
nodes.rationale: Near-term realistic application: human mathematicians use AI as computational assistant for subtasks while verifying outputs; mirrors trajectory in other domains; tools like Lean Copilot exemplify collaborative approach.

nodes.label: Moonshot Mathematics Vision
nodes.rationale: True moonshots require formulating conjectures, building novel frameworks, navigating unknown solution spaces; RIEMANN-BENCH is intermediate evaluation; reliable performance on research problems with known solutions prerequisite for open research contribution.

nodes.label: GSM8K: Grade-School Math Benchmark
nodes.author: Cobbe et al.
nodes.rationale: First mathematical reasoning benchmark for LLMs (2021); 8,500 grade-school problems requiring 2-8 steps; frontier models now exceed 90%, rendering benchmark saturated; established verifier-based evaluation paradigm.

nodes.label: MATH Dataset: Competition-Level Benchmark
nodes.author: Hendrycks et al.
nodes.rationale: 12,500 competition-level problems from AMC, AIME; best models achieved ~7% at introduction; frontier models now exceed 90%; demonstrates rapid saturation of competition-style benchmarks.

nodes.label: OmniMATH: Olympiad-Level Benchmark
nodes.author: Gao et al.
nodes.rationale: 4,428 problems across 33 sub-domains from USAMO, APMO, Putnam; targets olympiad-level difficulty; represents progression beyond competition-level benchmarks.

nodes.label: FrontierMath: Expert-Authored Research Benchmark
nodes.author: Glazer et al.
nodes.rationale: Hundreds of expert-authored problems spanning major areas of modern mathematics; initial report <2% performance; newer agentic systems improved to 48% on Tier 4; demonstrates progress but still substantial gap.

nodes.label: AlphaProof: Formal Theorem Proving System
nodes.author: Hubert et al.
nodes.rationale: Solved hardest problem at IMO 2024; scored 28/42 at IMO 2024 (silver medal); combined with AlphaGeometry 2 for geometry problems; demonstrates frontier of formal mathematical reasoning.

nodes.label: Gemini with Deep Think: Gold-Medal IMO Performance
nodes.rationale: First AI system officially certified at gold-medal standard by IMO coordinators (2025); scored 35/42 on IMO 2025; demonstrates frontier of olympiad-level performance.

nodes.label: DeepSeekMath-V2: High-Performance Mathematical Reasoning
nodes.author: Shao et al.
nodes.rationale: Gold-level performance on IMO 2025 and CMO 2024; scored 118/120 on Putnam 2024; demonstrates state-of-the-art olympiad-level reasoning.

nodes.label: OpenAI o1: Reasoning-Focused Model
nodes.rationale: Applies reinforcement learning to develop extended chains of reasoning; key driver of gains in mathematical problem-solving; represents paradigm shift toward reasoning-focused architectures.

nodes.label: DeepSeek-R1: Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning
nodes.author: Guo et al.
nodes.rationale: Applies reinforcement learning to develop extended reasoning chains; key driver of recent mathematical reasoning improvements; demonstrates effectiveness of reasoning-focused training.

nodes.label: AlphaGeometry: Geometry Problem Solving
nodes.author: Trinh et al.
nodes.rationale: Solved 25 of 30 historical IMO geometry problems; matched average gold medalist performance; specialized system for geometry domain.

nodes.label: Lean Copilot: Collaborative Theorem Proving
nodes.author: Song et al.
nodes.rationale: LLMs as copilots for theorem proving in Lean; exemplifies collaborative approach where humans verify AI outputs; realistic near-term application paradigm.

nodes.label: AxiomProver: Formal Putnam Solver
nodes.rationale: Solved all 12 problems from 2025 William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition in Lean 4.21.0; 8 solved during competition, 4 in following days; demonstrates formal theorem proving frontier.
